claims.claim: Best Start Grant is for eligible families in Scotland.
claims.quote: If you live in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, you cannot get Best Start Grant or Best Start Foods.
claims.note: The source excludes the other UK nations.

claims.claim: Pregnancy and Baby Payment is usually £398.35 for a later child, with exceptions.

claims.note: The source states the ordinary later-child rate and then lists exceptions to it.

claims.claim: Some later children may receive the higher Pregnancy and Baby Payment.
claims.quote: In some circumstances, you may be able to get extra support for a child that’s not your first. You may get the £796.65 payment if:

claims.claim: Early Learning Payment is £331.95.
claims.quote: If your application is successful you'll get £331.95 to help with the costs of early learning.
claims.note: The source states the amount.

claims.claim: School Age Payment is £331.95.
claims.quote: School Age Payment is a payment of £331.95 per child.
claims.note: The source states the amount.

claims.claim: Best Start Grant has three types of payment in Scotland for eligible families.
claims.quote: The 3 Best Start Grant payments are:
claims.note: The source identifies three payments and separately excludes other UK nations.

claims.claim: Normally the applicant or partner must get a qualifying benefit.
claims.quote: To get Best Start Grant and Foods, normally you or your partner need to get one of these: Universal Credit Housing Benefit Income Support Pension Credit income-based Jobseekers Allowance (JSA) income-related Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
claims.note: The source gives the ordinary listed-benefit condition.

claims.claim: An applicant under 18 can qualify without a qualifying benefit.
claims.quote: If you're under 18, you do not need to be on any payments or benefits to get Best Start Grant or Best Start Foods.
claims.note: The under-18 exception is explicit.

claims.claim: Some 18- or 19-year-olds can qualify without their own qualifying benefit.
claims.quote: If you're 18 or 19 and do not get any benefits or payments, you can still apply for Best Start Grant or Best Start Foods. Your parent or carer needs to get one of these for you: Child Benefit Universal Credit child payments the child addition part of Pension Credit
claims.note: The source requires a parent or carer to receive a listed payment for the young applicant.

claims.claim: An application can be made while a qualifying benefit decision is pending.
claims.quote: If you're not getting any of these benefits or payments, but have applied for one, you can still apply for Best Start Grant and Best Start Foods.
claims.note: The source permits applying after filing for a qualifying benefit.

claims.claim: Pregnancy and Baby Payment is usually £796.65 for a first child.
claims.quote: You'll get a Pregnancy and Baby Payment of £796.65 for your first child.
claims.note: The source states the ordinary first-child amount.

claims.claim: Pregnancy and Baby Payment is usually £398.35 for a later child.
claims.quote: This will change to a payment of £398.35 for any child that comes after your first.
claims.note: The source states the ordinary later-child amount.

claims.claim: A higher amount is possible for some later children.
claims.quote: In some circumstances, you may be able to get extra support for a child that’s not your first. You may get the £796.65 payment if:
claims.note: The source lists circumstances in which a later child gets the higher amount.

claims.claim: The usual Pregnancy and Baby Payment application window runs from the end of the 24th week of pregnancy until the baby is six months old.
claims.quote: You can get Pregnancy and Baby Payment any time after you have reached the end of the 24th week of pregnancy until the day your baby is 6 months old.
claims.note: The source states this ordinary window.

claims.claim: Premature birth can change the Pregnancy and Baby Payment application start date.
claims.quote: If your baby is born before 24 weeks, you can apply from this date up to the day your baby is 6 months old.
claims.note: The source allows applying from birth if birth precedes 24 weeks.

claims.claim: Taking over care can change the Pregnancy and Baby Payment application deadline.
claims.quote: If you've taken over looking after a child, for example, if you've adopted, you can apply up to the day before the child's first birthday.
claims.note: The source extends the deadline for a person taking over care.

claims.claim: Stillbirth or infant death gives different Pregnancy and Baby Payment application dates.
claims.quote: If you apply after a stillbirth or death, you can apply up to 6 months after the baby's birth date.
claims.note: The source expressly permits applying after stillbirth or death, but the stated six-month deadline is not different from the ordinary deadline.

claims.claim: Early Learning Payment is £331.95 when the child is aged 2 to 3½.
claims.quote: You can get the payment when your child is aged between 2 years old and 3 years and 6 months old.
claims.note: The same section gives the £331.95 amount.

claims.claim: School Age Payment is £331.95 in the year the child is first old enough to start school.
claims.quote: School Age Payment is a payment of £331.95 per child. It helps with the costs of preparing for school when your child is first old enough to start primary school.
claims.note: The source gives the amount and timing.
